newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells wine maker to employees for $6.5mln.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells wine maker to employees for $6.5mln.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Friday it has sold 78 percent of wine maker Vinprom Lyaskovets to a joint stock company set up by its staff for $6.52 million.
Lyaskovets sells sparkling wine, mainly to Russia and its table wines are sold in J. Sainsbury Plc and other chain stores in Great Britain. Over 80 percent of its output is exported.

Under the deal 10 percent of the price will be paid in cash on the day of signing of the contract and the remaining 90 percent in six equal annual instalments with one-year grace period, the agency said in a statement.
The buyer has also pledged to cover company debts of 2.5 billion levs ($1.6 million) and to invest $3.525 million in the company over the next three years.
Twenty percent of the remaining equity will be offered at preferential prices to its employees and two percent will be set aside to meet property claims by former pre-communist owners.
The buyer, Vinprom Lyaskovets 1934, is a joint stock company registered by 539 employees of Vinprom Lyaskovets, the statement said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188 ($ = 1569 Bulgarian Levs)
